card.title: Balanced Search Tree From a Sorted List

a1.cap: Build a height-balanced binary search tree from the sorted array nums. Always choose the middle element (lo + hi) / 2 (rounding down) of the current range as the root, so the answer is unique.
a1.say: Build a height-balanced binary search tree from the sorted array nums. Always choose the middle element (lo plus hi) over 2 (rounding down) of the current range as the root, so the answer is unique.

lines: Build a height-balanced binary search tree from the sorted array nums. Always choose the middle element (lo + hi) / 2 (rounding down) of the current range as the root, so the answer is unique.

a1.cap: For example, with nums = [-10,-3,0,5,9], the answer is [0,-10,5,null,-3,null,9].
a1.say: For example, with nums equals -10, -3, 0, 5, 9, the answer is 0, -10, 5, null, -3, null, 9.

a1.cap: The middle value splits the list into two halves of almost equal size. Make it the root, then build the left half into the left subtree and the right half into the right subtree. Balanced halves give a balanced tree.
Let's walk through it with nums = [-10,-3,0,5,9].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with nums equals -10, -3, 0, 5, 9.

a1.cap: The middle of positions 0 to 4 is 0: it becomes a root.
The middle of positions 0 to 1 is -10: it becomes a root.
a1.say: The middle of positions 0 to 1 is minus 10: it becomes a root.

a1.cap: The middle of positions 1 to 1 is -3: it becomes a root.
a1.say: The middle of positions 1 to 1 is minus 3: it becomes a root.

a1.cap: The middle of positions 3 to 4 is 5: it becomes a root.
The middle of positions 4 to 4 is 9: it becomes a root.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(log n).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of log n.

a1.cap: That's the Divide and Conquer approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
